results.reason: Cites Agmt §2.2 automatic five-year renewal and the 270–240 day window against June 30, 2027 (Oct. 3 – Nov. 2, 2026). Explains the lock-in for five years with a higher minimum, which runs to 2032. Recommends a protective non-renewal notice or a signed extension amendment before the deadline.

Explains the §5.3 30-day objection right and deemed acceptance. Notes Aug. 21 receipt and a deadline of about Sept. 20, says the right has almost certainly lapsed, and recommends confirming with the client whether a timely objection was sent and using leverage to negotiate.

Issue 5 says the §11.1 indemnity reaches product-defect claims and is uncapped, while §11.2 is narrow and capped. Recommends narrowing §11.1 to Halvorsen's own fault and adding §11.2 to the carve-outs.
Issue 4 says Amend. §3.1 deletes former §12.3(b), so Recall reimbursement is now capped at 12 months' payments and a recall could exceed it. Recommends reinstating the carve-out.
Issue 3 identifies Amend. §6 Delaware law and Wilmington forum, the conflict with Agmt §§17.1–17.2 New York, and that the Amendment prevails under §1.4. Recommends restoring New York law and forum.
States the Notice was delivered Aug. 21, 2026.
States the Initial Term ends June 30, 2027.
States the Amendment outranks the Agreement body under Agmt §1.4.
Formatted as a memo to the Supervising Partner, with Where, Why it matters, and Fix given for each issue.
Concludes the opposite: the recall reimbursement is now capped.
Expressly acknowledges that the Delaware provisions control.
